questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
Out of the box, his advice depends on the leather. For finished, smooth-leather Blundstones, he reports that Blundstone's FAQ advises against treating them out of the box, because they already come pretreated [1]. Rustic brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black styles are the exception: they don't get the same pretreatment, and the FAQ says they may be conditioned for extra weatherproofing [2]. For distressed pairs like his, he strongly recommends conditioning them and says he doesn't recommend keeping them dry [3].

On frequency, he doesn't give a fixed schedule. His newest view, from 2022, is to treat them when they need it: if they look dry, feel dry, or stop beating water off the top [5]. He admits he probably does too little [4]. In his 2019 review, he said heavy wear might mean waxing every month or even every week, though light wear needs much less [6]. His general rule is that leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should be conditioned [7].

Your boot style isn't stated in your question, so which of the out-of-box advice applies depends on whether your pair is smooth or distressed.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer: Not in a normal wash, according to The Iron Snail's most recent take on the 501 Shrink-to-Fit (2023). He says that a hot wash in the dryer would make them noticeably smaller, but an ordinary wash makes a difference so small he doubts you would ever notice [1][2]. He also thinks that wearing them frequently would stretch them out to about the same size as rinsed 501s [3]. The tight fit he got came from very hot water and no dryer, and he advises against putting STFs in the dryer or washing them that hot if you want a good fit [4]. His 2019 experience was different: after shrinking them himself, the waist was very tight, and a week later it had stretched enough that he could wear a belt [5][6].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer: For the 501 STF, The Iron Snail's advice is to size up from your usual size, not buy it. His most recent take is that you should usually go two sizes up in the waist [1]. Levi's guidance, as he relays it, is to go two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer than you would normally wear [2][3]. Applying his rule to a 33x30 gives roughly a 35 waist and a 32 length. He learned this the hard way: after buying a 29 waist he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe, and he said he would have gone to a 32 length [4]. He hasn't covered 502 sizing in these videos, so this is based only on his 501 STF advice.

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Mostly yes, in his 2022 review, but his most recent video has pulled back from that. In the 2022 review he called the Red Wing 3335s his favourite boots he has ever had and said they beat his 1907s [1]. He framed it as a matter of use: the 1907s are more heavily built, so for a truly tough boot he says the 3335s probably aren't the ones to get, though he calls them a dramatically better all-around boot for hikes and walking [2][3].

In his September 2023 video, he is selling the 3335s. He still says they might be his favourite Red Wings of all time, but he now hedges and says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [4]. He still likes the 3335s for being lighter and more nimble for walking or a light hike, but he is getting rid of them [5][6].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his late-2023 video, The Iron Snail was still a big fan of Blundstones, even while thinning out his boot collection. He says "bluntstones are just incredible" and that he's "a big fan of them" [1]. He's retiring his heavily worn Blundstone 585s, the pair from his first ever video, because they have held up well and stayed water resistant [2]. He's letting go of the Blundstone 989 Extreme work boots. He had thought they were waterproof, but he corrected himself: they are "a very very water resistant nubuck" [3]. He keeps a pair of slip-on Blundstones for quick errands, though he says he "could easily put them on the sell list" [4].

His view has been consistently positive over time. In 2022 he called Blundstones "still some of my favorites" [5], and after a year of wear in 2020 he said the boots were "still great boots" [6]. His earliest advice, from 2019, was that they're worth buying if you're willing to keep them treated [7].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail's clearest take on this is from his 2022 Dr. Martens guide, and he leans toward Solovair. He says that if you're going for pure value and want a better built boot, Solovair is where he'd point you[1][2][3], and he says he loves them[4]. He argues the extra money for Made in England Docs mostly pays for the Made in England part, which he says is about a third of the boot price[1]. On the leather, he says Made in England Docs' leather will age fine and that is probably on par with Solovair[5], and their midsoles are probably also on par with Solovair's[6]. Where they differ, he says Solovair is a much smaller company and one of the original makers of Doc Martens[7]. Solovairs have a shank, which Docs lack[8], so he says they are a bit more comfortable over long periods of time[9]. He says the derby eight-eyed Solovair is essentially the exact same boot as Docs[10], and the only thing Solovair doesn't do is the yellow stitching, so if that matters to you, he says you'd need Made in England Docs for the highest quality[11]. He recommends checking Solovair out[12]. He also reports a manufacturing defect on his own pair: a tab on the back ripped off the right boot after eight wears[13]. This is from 2022. His 2023 video compares Made in England and Made in Thailand Docs and doesn't cover Solovair.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail hasn't covered a multi-day hike like yours, or how the boots fare with a loaded pack over several days. His most recent view, from his one-year review, is that the rustic brown Blundstones handled plenty of hiking for him. He wore them every day for about eight months and went on a lot of hikes with them [1], including going up and down a few mountains in Maine, where they got a little scuffed but held up well [3]. His main caveat is that he says they are apparently not good for mountaineering because they lack ankle support [2], so that is the point to weigh for a 4-day trip on rough ground. He also says they are fine for crossing a brook or stream or standing in mud [4]. On water, his earlier advice was that the boots stay water resistant only if you keep them treated, and that untreated or old leather is not hydrophobic [5]. Since he hasn't addressed multi-day trips directly, treat his view as a day-hike endorsement with that ankle-support caveat.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer: For the best balance of cost and quality, the most recent view from The Iron Snail is Uniqlo's $20 tee. He calls it probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price [1]. In an earlier video he said the $15 Uniqlo has a bound neck collar so it doesn't wiggle, and called the price-to-quality ratio insane [2]. His own sizing rule points you past the Uniqlo, though. He says that if you're taller or wider, you'd want Muji [3]. It costs about $4 or $5 more, but it is significantly longer and a good deal wider [4]. At 5 foot 11 and 225 lbs, applying that rule to you points to Muji. If you want to spend more for a premium shirt with zero torque, he also rates House of Blanks at $35 [5]. He hasn't said what size he'd pick for your height and weight, so I can't give you a specific size. The closest thing he's said is that Muji's extra length and width suit bigger wearers.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail's most recent take (2023) is that the 875s and 1907s each have characteristics he likes, and he doesn't rank one above the other there [1]. The main difference he drew in his 2021 review is the welt. The 875 is Goodyear welted, which leaves space for cork that molds to your foot over time [2]. The 1907 adds a storm welt, which he calls invaluable [3]. He describes the popular view that Red Wing's storm welt is basically another strip of leather on the welt, though he says he isn't quite sure [4]. The 1907 also comes with a removable leather footbed, which he says you can typically buy separately for $40 [5], and leather laces, which he says typically cost $15 [6]. He says the 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 but argues the extras make it the better deal [7]. Those prices are from 2021 and may have changed. In his 2022 video, both use crepe soles [8], and he says the 875s and 1907s are more heavily built than his 3335s, so they're the better pick if you need a tough boot [9]. The Iron Snail hasn't covered in these videos how the two differ in fit or how they compare on durability in everyday use.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail's clearest budget pick is Uniqlo. In his newest video on this, he says a $20 Uniqlo tee is probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price [1]. In his June 2025 video, when the shirt was $15, he called it very good for the money and said the price-to-quality ratio was insane [2][3]. In an earlier video he said that if you want a heavyweight, coarse-feeling tee with a bound, ribbed collar, and are looking for the best bargain, this may be it [4]. Front General Store is his step-up pick at about $40. He calls it made in Japan and says it has great proportions and feel [5], and one of the best shirts you could possibly get [6]. It was pre-washed, with 1.2% width and 0% length shrinkage and a softness score of 6 out of 10 [7]. Pro Club is one he came to like, but he found it the roughest shirt on his list [8]. He measured it at 2.78% width and 6.86% length shrinkage, with softness 4 of 10 [9]. Hanes is a classic cheap basic. He says it is much softer than the lighter Pro Club [10], and calls it a classic $10 great shirt with softness 7 out of 10 [11][12]. He also said that in his June 2025 test, the low-price mass-market basics he had from big brands all had a defect [13]. Overall, his lean is Uniqlo for the best budget shirt, Hanes if you want something softer than Pro Club at a similar price, and Front General Store if you can spend about $40. He hasn't ranked all four head to head in a single video, so this comparison is pieced together from different videos and different shrink tests.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer: Assuming "this" means the Barbour, he would lean toward the Barbour for that mix, with caveats. In his newest comparison he calls the Barbour's 6 oz Sylkoil fabric the lightest of the jackets he covered [1], and says that flexibility means you could wear it any time of year [2]. The liners can be added for cold weather and taken out otherwise [3]. For rain, though, he says it isn't a designated rain jacket [4]. In his 2021 shower test it didn't leak [5], but he says these jackets are very water resistant only when properly treated [6], and water resistance drops as the wax wears [7]. The storm cuffs help in inclement weather [8]. For the Flint and Tinder, he says it's lined and a lighter weight that's comfortable [9][10], that it goes with anything [10], and that it's literally built for everyone [11]. That segment was a paid Huckberry sponsorship [12]. He hasn't covered rain or windbreaker use for either jacket, so I can't say which handles those better. Based on what he said, the Barbour fits the multi-season layering use better, while the Flint and Tinder is the simpler lined everyday option.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail isn't saying Huckberry only makes unlined jackets. His con is about the one he reviewed. In the 2023 video he calls the Huckberry jacket "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1], and his objection is personal: "I personally always like aligning on wax jackets" so the wax doesn't touch your clothes or arms [2]. He still says "chances are you will be happy with this jacket" [3], so he presents the lining point as a preference rather than a verdict on quality. In his 2025 video he discusses a lined Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker sold through Huckberry, saying "It's lined, so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin." [4] He also mentions a wool-lined version he hasn't tried yet: "They also make a really nice wool lined one that I'm yet to get" [5]. That segment was a paid sponsor read from Huckberry [6]. He doesn't mention a flannel-lined version, and he doesn't say whether the lined Flint and Tinder is the same product as the unlined 2023 jacket, so the unlined con applies to that jacket. His view on lining has softened with age: "I kind of see why you wouldn't line something" [7].

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer: The Iron Snail hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s with the 875s in these videos. He says the 3335s are true to size for him [1], but they have a slim, tapered profile, and with wool socks his toes felt squished [2]. When he compares the 875s to the 3335s, it's about build rather than fit: he calls the 875s and 1907s more beefily constructed, so for a tougher boot he suggests those instead [3]. For Red Wings in general, he advises buying leather boots snug rather than squished, since they conform to your feet over time [4].
